title: COLLABORATIVE EDITOR (GOOGLE DOCS)
subtitle: The challenge is correctness, not scale: everyone must end up with the same document.
footer: DDIA: Ch 5 conflict resolution · Ch 9 total order · Ch 11 event log   ·   Similar: Ride sharing · Live comments · Stock trading · Online auction

items: Send small operations, not whole documents; last-write-wins on documents loses people's work.
One server per document orders operations and transforms concurrent ones (OT); CRDTs are the serverless alternative.
Append every operation to a log before acknowledging it, and snapshot periodically for fast loading.
Create and open documents
Many users edit concurrently and see each other's changes live
See collaborators' cursors and presence
Remote edits visible < 100ms
All replicas converge to the same document
No lost edits (durable)
~100 concurrent editors per doc; millions of docs
Each keystroke is an op (~100B).
100 editors × 5 ops/s = 500 ops/s per hot doc, which one server handles easily.
The challenge is correctness, not scale.

Naive: send the whole document on save. Last write wins, and someone's work disappears.

items: Send operations (insert "x" at 5).
Every op is appended to the op log before it is acknowledged; periodic snapshots make loading fast (snapshot + tail).
All editors of a doc must reach the same owner server: consistent hashing on doc_id, with ownership coordinated through ZooKeeper.
OT or CRDT?
OT: a central server orders and transforms; compact; needs one coordinator per doc (Google Docs).
Why one server per doc?
OT needs a single total order of ops (DDIA Ch 9).
Offline edits?
Client buffers ops tagged with a base version; on reconnect the server transforms them against everything since that version.
Cursors?
Ephemeral presence over the same socket; not persisted.
Locking the document or paragraph, which defeats real-time collaboration.
Adding parts before a number shows they are needed.
Ignoring retries, timeouts and crashes.
